acceptance_criteria.criterion: No echo statements remain in ModuleInfoParser
YAML parse errors return null with BuildMessages::addError() instead of re-throwing exceptions
Missing/incomplete moduleMetaData uses BuildMessages::addWarning() instead of echo
ModulesOverviewGenerator continues to work correctly (already handles null returns)

summary: Replaced `echo` + `throw $e` in the ParseException catch block with `BuildMessages::addError()` + `return null;`.
Replaced both `echo` warning statements (missing moduleMetaData section and incomplete moduleMetaData) with `BuildMessages::addWarning()` calls.
Updated the `parseFile()` docblock to reflect the new non-fatal error behaviour.
All 5 ModulesOverviewGenerator tests pass. PHPStan error is pre-existing in DBHelper/FetchMany.php — not introduced by this change.

comments.note: The `ParseException` import in `ModuleInfoParser.php` remains correct — the exception is still caught (just no longer re-thrown), so the import is still needed.
The pre-existing PHPStan error in `src/classes/DBHelper/FetchMany.php` (return type incompatibility on `fetch()`) is unrelated to this WP but should be addressed separately.

summary: All four acceptance criteria verified by code inspection and runtime execution.
AC1: grep confirms zero `echo` statements remain in ModuleInfoParser.php.
AC2: EC1 edge-case test — invalid YAML triggers BuildMessages::addError() and returns null (no exception propagates).
AC3: EC2/EC3/EC4 edge-case tests — missing or incomplete moduleMetaData triggers BuildMessages::addWarning() and returns null in all variants.
AC4: ModulesOverviewGeneratorTest (5 tests, 10 assertions) and ModulesOverviewRendererTest (9 tests, 21 assertions) both pass cleanly under PHP 8.5.4.
Additional edge-case confirmed: moduleMetaData present as a YAML scalar (not array) is correctly rejected with a warning and null return.

comments.note: The deprecated `$http_response_header` notices from vendor/shark/simple_html_dom.php appear on every test run. These are pre-existing, unrelated to this WP, but could be suppressed or the library updated to silence PHP 8.5 deprecation noise.
No improvement: code is clean, all error paths return null and register diagnostics correctly. BuildMessages::reset() is available for test isolation — the implementation is testable by design.

summary: Code review PASS. Single file change (ModuleInfoParser.php) is clean, minimal, and correctly scoped. All three echo-to-BuildMessages replacements are accurate: addError() for the ParseException path (non-fatal, returns null), addWarning() for missing/incomplete moduleMetaData (both guards). BuildMessages API called with correct two-argument signature (source, message) matching the convenience shorthands. The combined guard `!is_array($data) || !isset($data['moduleMetaData']) || !is_array($data['moduleMetaData'])` correctly collapses three distinct null/missing/scalar cases into one path; the message text is consistent with all three scenarios. No behavioral changes to resolveSourcePath, resolveComposerPackageName, or resolveContextOutputFolder. All project conventions observed: array() syntax, declare(strict_types=1), final class, correct namespace and use ordering.

comments.note: The source-label string 'ModuleInfoParser' is hard-coded as a literal in all three BuildMessages calls. A private class constant (e.g. `private const SOURCE = 'ModuleInfoParser';`) would eliminate the triple duplication and make a future rename a single-point change. Not blocking — the class is `final` and the string is stable, but worth a follow-up tidy-up.

[documentation-forward] The updated parseFile() docblock correctly reflects the non-fatal behaviour, but the module's .context/ overview (if one exists) and any BuildMessages integration notes should mention that ModuleInfoParser now routes all diagnostic output through BuildMessages rather than stdout. This ensures future contributors know not to expect echo output from this parser during builds.

notes: All four acceptance criteria are met. The `ModulesOverviewGenerator` test suite (5 tests, 10 assertions) passes cleanly.

All 4 ACs are met and verified by runtime edge-case tests.
